content: Do not take irbesartan and hydrochlorothiazide if you are pregnant. If you become pregnant while using this medication, contact your doctor immediately, as it can harm the developing fetus. Irbesartan belongs to a class of drugs called angiotensin II receptor antagonists, which work by blocking certain natural substances that tighten blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more easily. Hydrochlorothiazide is a diuretic, commonly referred to as a water pill, which helps the kidneys eliminate excess water and salt through urine. This medication is available in tablet form and is typically taken once daily, with or without food. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully. If you have any questions, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Take the medication exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. It may take 2 to 4 weeks to experience its full benefits. Continue taking it even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other purposes. If you have questions about its use, ask your doctor or pharmacist. Before starting this medication, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to irbesartan, hydrochlorothiazide, sulfa drugs, or any other substances. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are taking.g. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. Inform your doctor if you are on dialysis or if you have a history of asthma, lupus, diabetes, heart failure, gout, or kidney or liver disease. Let your doctor know if you are breastfeeding. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Discuss the safe use of alcohol with your doctor, as alcohol can exacerbate side effects. This medication may also cause dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting, especially when standing up quickly. To minimize this, rise slowly from a lying position. Consult your doctor before using potassium-containing salt substitutes. If your doctor recommends a low-salt or low-sodium diet or an exercise program, follow these instructions carefully. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. This medication may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience dizziness, extreme fatigue, upset stomach, vomiting, stomach pain, heartburn, chest pain, or flu-like symptoms. Serious side effects, though rare, require immediate medical attention. These include dry mouth, excessive thirst, weakness, lack of energy, restlessness, confusion, seizures, muscle pain or cramps, infrequent urination, rapid heartbeat, lightheadedness, or fainting. Report any unusual symptoms to your doctor. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA's MedWatch program. Store this medication in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance. In case of overdose, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments while taking this medication. Your doctor may order tests to monitor your response to the treatment. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refills, consult your pharmacist. This medication is sold under the brand name Avalide®.
